pairs.question: Tantane, omnipotens, caligine mersa latere fata placet?
pairs.answer: ueniet quondam felicior aetas, cum pia Campano gaudebit consule Roma et per bella diu fasces perque arma negatos ultro ad magnanimos referet secura nepotes.
pairs.derivation: Authorial apostrophe to Jupiter: the poet asks whether it pleases the almighty that the fates lie hidden in such darkness, then answers his own question with the prophecy of a happier age. Question span ends at 'fata placet?' (full stop). Answer begins at 'ueniet' (the operative answering sentence) and stops at the first full stop, 'nepotes.'; what follows ('poena superborum tamen haec durabit auorum...') is further elaboration on Capua's punishment, not part of the direct answer. Inline every-5-lines verse numbers (123, 125, 126) stripped from mid-line.
